subject: Draft MAP: Data handling & compliance milestones (Healthlytics)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -0000
Subject: Draft MAP: Data handling & compliance milestones (Healthlytics)

Hi Sara / Tom —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) focused on the data handling & compliance milestone we discussed. I summarized the milestones, suggested owners, target dates, and dependencies below so we have a single place to iterate. Please review and flag anything missing or incorrect.

Summary of MAP items (data handling & compliance):

1) Security questionnaire / artifact delivery
   - Owner: Healthlytics (request) / Redwood (provide)
   - Deliverables: Completed security questionnaire, SOC 2 Type II report (redacted), encryption architecture diagram
   - Target date: 2026-02-26
   - Dependencies: Healthlytics to confirm required artifact scope (PHI scope?)

2) Data classification & retention policy alignment
   - Owner: Healthlytics (policy) / Redwood (configuration guidance)
   - Deliverables: Retention window agreement, retention configuration in Redwood Console, data deletion process
   - Target date: 2026-03-05
   - Dependencies: Confirmation of which datasets contain PHI/PII and legal retention requirements

3) Logging, audit trails, and access controls
   - Owner: Redwood (implementation) / Healthlytics (access lists)
   - Deliverables: Audit log samples, RBAC setup, KMS integration plan, access review cadence
   - Target date: 2026-03-12
   - Dependencies: KMS key details, list of admin/readonly users, Clarify retention period for logs (90/365 days?)

4) PHI/PII handling constraints & minimization plan
   - Owner: Healthlytics (requirements) / Redwood (technical controls + contractual language)
   - Deliverables: Accepted data minimization approach, agreed redaction/obfuscation rules, inbound data filtering rules
   - Target date: 2026-03-10
   - Dependencies: Healthlytics legal to confirm PHI scope and any HIPAA BAA needs

5) Final sign-off & pilot start
   - Owner: Healthlytics Product / Redwood Customer Success
   - Deliverables: Signed MAP, pilot kickoff schedule
   - Target date: 2026-03-20

Next steps (for you):
- Review attached MAP PDF and the security questionnaire (xlsx).
- Confirm which data streams will be considered PHI/PII and the primary contact for legal/compliance.
- Confirm whether Healthlytics requires a BAA.

Rishi and Neha are looped on technical and CS questions. If this scope looks good I’ll update the MAP and share a tracked-change version.

Attachments: MAP-draft-Healthlytics-20260218.pdf, security-questionnaire-HLTH-2026.xlsx

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0187

From: Sara Lind <sara.lind@healthlytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@healthlytics.com>, procurement@healthlytics.com
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 13:47:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Draft MAP: Data handling & compliance milestones (Healthlytics)

Marissa —

Thanks for the thorough recap and the draft MAP. A few quick clarifications from our side:

- PHI scope: We ingest EHR export files and some free-text clinical notes; those are in-scope for PHI. We will confirm the exact fields and send a sample data inventory by end of day Friday.
- Retention: Our legal prefers 7 years for clinical records, but we may be flexible on aggregated embeddings. Need to understand Redwood's retention controls for token/embedding storage and audit logs.
- Audit logs: We need immutable audit trails for all data access and admin configuration changes. Can you confirm log retention options and whether logs can be exported to our SIEM?
- BAA: We require a BAA for any PHI processing — is that something Redwood supports out of the box?

We’ll look through the security questionnaire and share the procurement contact separately.

Best,
Sara Lind
Director, Data & Security
Healthlytics, Inc.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lind <sara.lind@healthlytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 10:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Draft MAP: Data handling & compliance milestones (Healthlytics)

Hi Sara —

Appreciate the clarifications — this is helpful. Per your asks below, I updated the MAP and added concrete items for logging export, retention windows, and BAA steps. High-level answers to your questions here, and I’ve noted follow-ups in the MAP PDF (attached).

- PHI / BAA: Redwood supports BAAs for customers that need HIPAA protections. We have an established BAA process; I’ll loop Legal once you confirm you want Redwood to initiate.

- Retention controls: Redwood can configure per-route and per-model retention windows. For raw inputs we recommend a default 30-day retention for non-PHI and custom retention for PHI datasets (7 years) via customer-configured policies. We can implement policy-based retention that will auto-delete data and remove KV cache entries after the configured window. This will be a pre-production configuration (we will not delete customer-side data without sign-off).

- Audit logs & exports: We provide detailed, tamper-evident audit logs capturing request metadata (timestamp, route, model, token counts, requester id), admin configuration changes, and user access events. Logs can be retained for configurable periods (90/365/730 days) and exported to your SIEM via secure S3 push or syslog endpoint. For HIPAA use cases we recommend 365+ days; we can support 7 years if required.

- KMS/HSM & encryption: We support customer-managed keys (KMS) across AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and can integrate with HSM-backed providers. All at-rest and in-transit encryption defaults are applied.

Updated MAP highlights (new/changed):
- Added step: BAA execution -> Owner: Healthlytics Legal / Redwood Legal -> Target date: 2026-02-28
- Log export configuration workshop -> Owner: Redwood SE (Rishi) / Healthlytics (security) -> Target date: 2026-02-24
- Retention policy sign-off for PHI -> Owner: Healthlytics Legal -> Target date: 2026-03-01

Immediate asks from Redwood to keep momentum:
1) Please send a redacted sample data inventory (fields + example rows) so we can scope PHI field mapping (due 2026-02-20).
2) Confirm whether Healthlytics wants Redwood to start the BAA intake (yes/no).
3) Identify SIEM endpoint preference for log export (S3 bucket or syslog) and point-of-contact for the export workshop.

Rishi — can you prepare a short runbook and log-export checklist for the workshop? Vivek, can you confirm if any additional artifacts (beyond SOC 2 and the encryption diagram) would help speed legal review?

Thanks — I’ll update the MAP once I have the sample inventory and your BAA confirmation.

Best,
Marissa
